transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (BrightGrid Head of TechOps), Priya Nair (BrightGrid Security), Luis Ortega (BrightGrid ML Eng), Dana Wu (BrightGrid Procurement)

Summary:
Quick weekly check-in on POC metrics, tuning we've applied, and security/compliance gating items for signoff. Main items: SSO test plan, audit-log retention and access, SOC2 attestation requests, and follow-up on model latency/cost improvements from batching and KV cache tuning.

Topics covered:
- Pilot performance metrics & recent tuning
- SSO/SAML integration progress + SCIM mapping notes
- Audit logs: format, retention windows, and access controls
- SOC2 / compliance evidence and where Redwood stands
- Next steps for pilot completion checklist

Shared artifacts referenced:
- https://drive.redwood.company/brightgrid/pilot_metrics.csv (latency/cost CSV - redacted link)
- security_pack_v2.pdf (shared in chat)
- SOC2_summary_2024.pdf (link)
- pilot-arch.png (diagram of VPC tunnel + KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Samantha: Hi everyone! thanks for joining, we'll keep to an hour, we've got a tight agenda. I think we left off last week with the SSO token issue and the audit log retention question. Is that right Tom?
[00:00:18] Tom: Yeah thats right. We did the staging deploy, we saw some request spikes when Luis ran the batch generator, so wanted to review the metrics and also making sure the security bits are green.
[00:00:30] Priya: Quick callout, for legal we need the logs retained for either 90 or 365 days, legal hasn't chosen yet but we need to know if Redwood can support both and whether logs can be kept inside our VPC.
[00:00:45] Samantha: Absolutely. Redwood can do two things: we stream audit logs out to your collector (Can be inside VPC using our sidecar) or we can hand you S3-compatible bundles. Retention is configurable, default is 90 days, we support custom retention to 365 days for Dedicated / Private deployments.
[00:01:04] Luis: Sorry, when you say "sidecar" do you mean the agent that runs in the private subnet? Will logs traverse the internet?
[00:01:14] Ravi: Good question. For Private/VPC we can keep egress limited. The agent forwards over your peering to the collector; by default nothing leaves the peering except the encrypted stream to your SIEM. If you use Hosted, log streaming goes to Redwood-managed S3 unless you opt into VPC export.
[00:01:30] Tom: Ok that's fine. Priya, will legal accept peering?
[00:01:36] Priya: They prefer nothing leaves our environment but peering with strict ACLs is usually okay, still need the written attestation.
[00:01:44] Samantha: We'll include that wording in the security pack.
[00:01:50] Dana: On procurement — can we get a note on whether SOC2 is current, or if it's just in progress? Our vendor onboarding needs the attestation.
[00:01:58] Samantha: Redwood has a SOC2 Type II report for the inference platform dated Q4 2024, I'll attach the excerpt and the redacted report. For Private installs we have supplementary docs about control mapping.
[00:02:15] Tom: Cool, please include the mapping to our control list. Also we had a hiccup in the SSO flow last week when accounts with long attribute names failed provisioning.
[00:02:27] Samantha: Right — Ravi, can you summarize the fix?
[00:02:30] Ravi: Sure. So what happened — and I'm paraphrasing because the transcript might be messy — the SAML assertion used a very long displayName attribute which exceeded our SCIM mapping length in the staging service. It truncated and caused a mismatch on the external id. We patched the SCIM mapping to use a shorter externalId field and added a guard for >64 chars. That is deployed to staging now.
[00:02:52] Priya: Nice. We'll try provisioning a test user after this call. We'll add two test accounts, one with long names to validate the guard.
[00:03:00] Samantha: Sounds good.
[00:03:05] Luis: on the perf side — Ravi sent the latency CSV, I pulled 10k requests from last night: median p95 is down from 420ms to 305ms after the KV cache changes but cost per 1k tokens is up slightly due to smaller batches.
[00:03:20] Ravi: Right — the tradeoff. We increased cache hit ratio by switching to prefix caching and warming for the common prompts; that reduces compute but increased small tail latency for the long-tail requests. We suggested switching to dynamic batching: aggressive during off-peak, conservative at peak hours. The figures in the CSV show estimated 12-18% cost savings overall if you accept a 25ms median latency increase in peak windows.
[00:03:48] Tom: Can we get those numbers by route? We need to show product teams the impact on the customer-facing experience.
[00:03:56] Samantha: Ravi will export route-level CSVs and also annotate which model variants were used.
[00:04:02] Ravi: Yep, I'll include per-route p50/p95/p99 and token-cost columns.
[00:04:08] [00:12:12] 
[00:12:12] Priya: Back to logs — can we confirm log formats? We need immutable audit trails that include user id, request id, model_version, and response hash for data lineage.
[00:12:22] Samantha: Our audit schema includes timestamp, request_id, user_id (if present), model_id, model_version, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, and a response_digest. We'll send the schema in the security pack; note sometimes the auto-transcription calls it KV "cash" or KV "cache" — so ignore that in the CSV.
[00:12:44] Tom: And access controls on logs — who at Redwood can view raw responses?
[00:12:50] Ravi: Only a narrow ops role for debugging; for Hosted we redact PII by default and store hashed digests. For Dedicated/Private you control access via RBAC and KMS policies. We can configure HSM-backed KMS so keys never leave your control.
[00:13:06] Priya: Good. We also need to know the retention timeline for raw response bodies versus metadata. Legal is more strict about raw bodies.
[00:13:16] Samantha: We recommend keeping metadata (audit events) for the full retention window and raw response bodies for a shorter window — typical pattern is metadata 365 days, raw responses 30–90 days depending on sensitivity. We'll flag that in the control mapping doc.
[00:13:34] Luis: For the POC metrics: we've been using the 7B open model, quantized int8. Any downside to switching to a 13B quantized variant for a subset of traffic to measure quality delta?
[00:13:46] Ravi: You can. The tradeoff is roughly 1.8x inference cost and slightly higher tail latency. But Redwood supports model routing so you can send a sample slice of traffic to the 13B and compare pass/fail on your evals. We can add that to the canary route.
[00:13:59] Tom: Let's do that for the analytics route — 5% traffic to 13B for a week.
[00:14:05] Samantha: Noted. We'll schedule that as a canary.
[00:14:12] [00:23:40] 
[00:23:40] Dana: Procurement — we need a simple statement: will pilot data be used for model training? Legal is insistent.
[00:23:48] Samantha: By default Redwood does not use customer prompts or responses to train models unless there is an opt-in contract. For Hosted that is a separate opt-in; for Dedicated/Private nothing is shared back. We'll include the explicit non-training clause in the contract addendum.
[00:23:58] Dana: Perfect.
[00:24:04] Priya: One more security detail: can audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM in real-time or do you only do batched exports?
[00:24:12] Ravi: We support both. Real-time streaming via Kinesis/Events or syslog over TLS for on-prem SIEMs, or batched S3 exports nightly. For high-security customers we often do both with real-time alerts for anomalous patterns.
[00:24:26] Priya: Ok we'll request real-time forwarding for our SOC team.
[00:24:31] Samantha: We'll include the forwarding playbook in the pack.
[00:24:36] [00:33:05] 
[00:33:05] Tom: On the SSO test: Priya will send SAML metadata and two test accounts; can we run a provisioning test on Wed?
[00:33:14] Priya: Wednesday works. We'll use the staging environment and mark accounts with long and normal attributes.
[00:33:20] Samantha: Ravi will meet you for the test. We'll also capture the debug logs and share the sanitized trace.
[00:33:27] Ravi: I will also bring tooling to simulate the higher QPS that caused the earlier spike so we can validate CPU throttling/queueing behavior.
[00:33:36] Luis: about throttling, can Redwood surface token-level billing tied to routes for us? We want to allocate costs by product feature.
[00:33:44] Samantha: Yes, Redwood Console supports token-level breakdown by route and model_id. We'll send a screenshot of the Console view and the API call to pull that CSV.
[00:33:54] Tom: Great.
[00:34:00] [00:44:12] 
[00:44:12] Priya: Are there any outstanding blockers that would prevent us from running the pilot to completion in two weeks?
[00:44:19] Samantha: Biggest items are: SSO provisioning test (we have a patch but need your SAML metadata), final confirmation on log retention and whether logs must remain in-VPC, and cost delta approval if you want to enable 13B canary. None are showstoppers.
[00:44:35] Tom: Sounds manageable. We'll prioritize SAML metadata and retention policy this week.
[00:44:40] Samantha: Great. I'll follow up with the security pack and the annotated CSV from Ravi.
[00:44:47] Dana: From procurement, please include billing terms for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot: monthly seat/commit estimates and options to convert to reserved capacity.
[00:44:58] Samantha: Will do. I'll work with finance to add that to the pilot quote.
[00:45:04] [00:53:00] 
[00:53:00] Closing recap (Samantha):
- Redwood to send security_pack_v2.pdf, SOC2 excerpt, and the SSO playbook (Samantha)
- Ravi to export route-level latency/cost CSV and propose batching config (Ravi)
- Priya to share SAML metadata and test creds for Wednesday (Priya)
- Tom to confirm retention window and VPC egress policy (Tom)
- Dana to confirm procurement acceptance items for pilot terms (Dana)

Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene next Monday at the same time unless we need a mid-week SSO test follow-up.

End of transcript.
